edge.title: The big order with no money yet
edge.setup: A buyer you have never dealt with asks for a large lot at a good rate. They want delivery first and promise payment later: a cheque, a transfer 'by evening', or 'once we sell it on'. Perhaps a small earlier order was paid on time, which is why this one feels safe.
edge.tell: A new buyer who wants the goods first and the money later is asking you to be their lender.
move: Release goods only against money that has cleared in your own account, not a screenshot, a cheque or a promise.
Keep first deals small and split large lots into instalments, each released after the previous one is paid.
Check the firm through an independent source, and call the number you find yourself rather than the one they gave you.
If it goes wrong, file a police complaint quickly with the chats, invoices and vehicle details.
edge.why: Credit fraud works because the seller's wish for volume overrides the ordinary question of whether this stranger is good for the money. A small early order paid on time buys trust cheaply, and the large one is where the fraudster collects. The defence is to treat every unpaid delivery as a loan and decide whether you would lend that much to that person.
edge.variants: Same shape: a freelancer asked to deliver the full work before any advance, a shop asked to hand over stock on 'consignment', a landlord handing over keys against a promised deposit.
edge.anchor: A firm has vanished without paying Rs 39 lakh for a bulk pepper purchase in a reported fraud case (Times of India, Bengaluru).

lens.name: Selection effects
lens.one_line: How a group got assembled usually explains the result better than anything about its members.
lens.detail: A survey of app users can't tell you about people who deleted it. Hospital data on a disease overrepresents severe cases, because mild ones never came. Online reviews over-sample the delighted and the furious. Before accepting a comparison between two groups, the first question is always how each group came to be in the sample.
elsewhere: 'Our customers love us' — the unhappy ones already left.
Exam toppers from a coaching centre that only admits toppers.
Crime statistics shaped by which complaints get registered.
lens.test: How did these people end up in this group — and who never had the chance to?
lens.today: Times of India reports tomato prices in Bengaluru have crashed by up to 80%, and in the same line says the drop is not city-wide. The 80% is the best case among the markets that were looked at, not what your local vendor charges. Treat any 'up to' figure as the edge of a selected sample, and check your own market before deciding how much to buy.

moved.what: About 1.3 lakh consumers have refused to share documents and opted out of the Jyothi power scheme (Times of India).
moved.so_what: Check on your electricity bill or your provider's app whether your connection is still covered before assuming the benefit continues; opting out of document sharing may mean opting out of the scheme.

moved.what: Tomato prices have crashed by up to 80% in parts of Bengaluru, though not city-wide (Times of India), while Dasara has pushed up flower and fruit prices (Urban Acres).
moved.so_what: Compare two or three vendors before buying, and buy tomatoes now rather than flowers or fruit if you have a choice.

moved.what: The inaugural Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper run is likely on 1 November (Deccan Herald, Times of India, Moneycontrol).
moved.so_what: Dates are still 'likely', so watch IRCTC for fares and booking opening before committing to Mumbai travel around that week.

moved.what: Metro commuters are asking about unused balance in smart cards as NCMC adoption grows (The Hindu).
moved.so_what: Load only what you will use in a few weeks, and check your card issuer's refund terms before topping up a large amount.

moved.what: Liquor sales curbs apply from 21 October for Dasara processions and MLC polls (Times of India).
moved.so_what: If you are hosting or buying for the festival, buy before the 21st; also expect procession traffic and diversions on that day.

carry_over.prompt: You are working in a café with your bag hanging behind your chair: what is the tell that your valuables are exposed?
carry_over.answer: If your wallet or phone is in a pocket or bag you cannot see or feel, it is available to anyone who walks past.
